exposure: Reversible bilateral uterine artery blockade with hysterolaparoscopy
Internal iliac artery blockade with hysterolaparoscopy
outcome: Maximum human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels (baseline, no difference)
Gestational tissue size on ultrasound imaging (no difference)
Occurrence of adverse pregnancy outcome (no association)
cohort: The study included patients diagnosed with cesarean scar pregnancy who underwent combined surgical intervention involving hysteroscopy and laparoscopy between May 2020 and February 2024.
finding: The uterine artery blockade group exhibited superior efficacy in the removal of scar pregnancies compared to the internal iliac artery blockade group, demonstrating shorter operative time, less bleeding, fewer hospital days, lower costs, and improved patient outcomes including quality of life and subsequent pregnancy rates.
